Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. Branch: feature/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches (already checked out, clean, based on origin/develop @269d5d4). Do NOT stage or commit anything — the skill commits, not you.

Implement Step 1 of the SFCC-91 build plan (full plan at /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-91/plan.md, section "## 4. Steps" → "### Step 1"). Touch exactly one file: overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx. Nothing else.

Context: this file is a 1069-line faithful copy-first TypeScript port of the base SFCC product-view component. It already has one precedent for this exact pattern — a `renderHeader` optional prop added in commit 227171e. Read that commit (`git show 227171e`) before you start so your new prop matches its shape and reasoning exactly.

What to do, in order:

1. Add a new optional prop to `ProductViewProps`, immediately after the existing `renderHeader` prop (~line 178):
   ```ts
   renderVariationAttribute?: (attr: SfccVariationAttribute) => React.ReactNode;
   ```
   Write a JSDoc comment on it that states the fall-through contract explicitly: return `undefined` to fall through to the base rendering. Returning `null` ALSO falls through and is not a way to render nothing — this is a real trap, document it so nobody discovers it the hard way.

2. Find the current variation-rendering loop (currently around lines 785-848): `variationAttributes.map(({ id, name, selectedValue, values }: SfccVariationAttribute) => { ... })`, which builds a `swatches` array and returns a `<SwatchGroup>`. Extract that ENTIRE loop body VERBATIM into a new function declared inside the component body, just above the component's `return (` statement (around line 688):
   ```ts
   const renderDefaultVariationAttribute = (attr: SfccVariationAttribute) => {
     const { id, name, selectedValue, values } = attr;
     // ...the exact same body that's currently in the .map() callback, unchanged...
   };
   ```
   It must be declared INSIDE the component function body (not at module scope), because it closes over `intl` (from `useIntl()`) and the `onVariationChange` prop from the component's own scope. The move must be byte-for-byte identical apart from the destructure moving from map-callback-params into the function body — do not reformat, do not touch comments, do not change any logic. This specifically includes:
   - Both `// audit-allow: verbatim from base product-view (...)` comments — they must survive unchanged.
   - The line doing `backgroundColor={name.toLowerCase()}` — must survive unchanged (this is base behaviour on this file; a *different*, new component elsewhere will deliberately not carry it, but that's out of scope for you — do not touch this file's behaviour here).
   - The `<Swatch>` and `<SwatchGroup>` JSX exactly as-is.

3. Do NOT add a default value at the prop destructure (unlike `renderHeader`, which does have one) — this default can't be expressed as a single JSX default in the parameter list, so the prop stays `undefined`-by-default and the call site (next step) handles the fall-through.

4. Replace the call site — the `variationAttributes.map(...)` — with:
   ```tsx
   variationAttributes.map((attr: SfccVariationAttribute) => (
     <React.Fragment key={attr.id}>
       {renderVariationAttribute?.(attr) ?? renderDefaultVariationAttribute(attr)}
     </React.Fragment>
   ))
   ```
   Use `React.Fragment` via the existing default `React` import at the top of the file (`import React, {forwardRef, useEffect, useMemo, useRef, useState, useCallback} from 'react';`) — do NOT add `Fragment` to that named-import list, reference it as `React.Fragment`. A keyed Fragment emits no DOM, so rendered output must be byte-identical to before this change. The `key={id}` that already exists on the inner `<SwatchGroup>` stays where it is (it's part of the verbatim-moved body) — it becomes redundant with the new Fragment key but that's fine, don't remove it since the body must stay verbatim.

5. Correct the file's header doc-comment (near the top of the file, lines ~19-21). It currently asserts something like "exactly one additive optional prop over the base file's surface — `renderHeader`" — after your change that sentence is factually wrong because there are now two such props. Rewrite it to name BOTH `renderHeader` and `renderVariationAttribute`, and repeat the same three-part justification pattern the existing text uses (behaviour-preserving default, zero occurrences of the new prop name in the base package, none of the base package's importers of this component are affected).

WHY this shape (so you can make good judgment calls if something doesn't quite match): the goal is a render slot that lets a caller override ONLY the colour-attribute's rendering while every other attribute (critically, the size attribute, which shares this exact code path today) renders completely unchanged via the same base markup. That's why the slot is per-attribute-in-the-loop rather than replacing the whole loop or the whole block — a future caller will pass a function that checks `attr.id === 'color'` and returns something custom only for that case, returning `undefined` for everything else so size falls through untouched.

Hard constraints:
- Touch ONLY overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx. Do not touch any other file.
- Do not reformat, do not remove or edit any existing comment other than the one header paragraph named in step 5, do not tighten or loosen any existing type.
- Do not run tsc, lint, test, or audit:tokens yourself — report back with a summary of exactly what you changed (function/line locations) and I will run the gates myself.
- Never stage (`git add`) or commit. Leave the change in the working tree.

Report back: a summary of the diff shape (which regions changed, roughly how many lines), and confirmation that the loop body was moved verbatim (quote the `audit-allow` comments and the `backgroundColor` line as they now appear, so I can visually confirm nothing drifted).

commit 227171e082c855c1fbfd367d12e30e71198e84f6
Author: Marcel Angelo Navarro <marcel.a.n.navarro@accenture.com>
Date:   Wed Aug 26 09:30:41 2026 +0800

    feat(product-view): add renderHeader slot for caller-supplied header content
    
    Adds one optional prop to ProductView so a caller can supply the header block, and
    corrects two documentation claims in the same file that were false or misleading.
    
    The slot
    ---------
    renderHeader?: (props: ProductViewHeaderProps) => React.ReactNode
    
    Its default renders the same private ProductViewHeader the base file renders inline, with
    the identical six values, so omitting it is behaviour-preserving. Both header call sites
    route through it — base renders the header twice behind responsive display arrays, and a
    slot only one of them honoured would be a silent half-override.
    
    Prop, default and call sites are one atomic unit, not three separable edits: deleting the
    default alone produces TS2722 at both call sites.
    
    Why the default export rather than a named-export wrapper
    ----------------------------------------------------------
    overrideStyling.md prescribes putting Zimmermann-only additions behind a named export that
    wraps the default. That route cannot express this requirement: a wrapper can only set props
    the default already accepts, so letting a caller replace an internal render block still
    requires the slot on the default. The only alternative is forking the component body, which
    is a graver breach of the faithful-port rule.
    
    The rule's stated purpose is served. renderHeader has zero occurrences in the base package,
    and the four base modules that import product-view — product-view-modal/index.jsx,
    product-view-modal/bundle.jsx, bonus-product-view-modal/index.jsx and
    pages/product-detail/index.jsx — neither pass it nor are affected by it. forwardRef
    behaviour is unchanged.
    
    Note overrideStyling.md cites product-tile/index.tsx (CardBaseline) and link/index.tsx as
    established precedent for the named-export split. Neither exists in overrides/, and
    CardBaseline appears nowhere in the codebase. Raised separately.
    
    Documentation corrections
    --------------------------
    The header's list of differences from base was exhaustive and became false the moment the
    prop landed; it is now scoped to name the addition.
    
    ProductViewRefScope's JSDoc told consumers to assert Ref<T> at the prop site. That is not
    required — TypeScript accepts the this-typed callback as a ref unaided, verified by removing
    the equivalent assertion and observing a clean typecheck against a live probe. The guidance
    sat in a shared component, so it propagated. It is now descriptive.
    
    Three inert casts removed
    --------------------------
    The cloneElement trio narrowed nothing: customButton.props is any, since React.ReactElement
    defaults P = any, and Partial<unknown> is {}. typescript.md reserves `as` for genuinely
    overriding inference, so documenting them would not have cured them. Removed with the
    comment that existed only to explain them; that block is now byte-identical to base
    index.jsx:493-503 modulo house formatting.
    
    Verified: tsc 0 - vitest 354/22 - lint 17 err/16 warn (baseline) - storybook 22 suites -
    audit:tokens 14 unack/21 ack, the five acknowledged literals intact and their windows
    re-checked after the line shift.
    
    Refs: SFCC-89.

1	# SFCC-91 — Build plan
2	
3	**Story:** PDP UI — Colour Swatches & Variation Selection
4	**Branch:** `feature/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches` (deliberately not the other developer's branch name)
5	**Baseline:** `develop` @ `269d5d4` — `tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run test` 26 files / 408 tests green
6	**Architecture:** per-attribute render slot on `product-view`. Decided by Marcel 2026-08-31. Not revisited.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## 1. Goal
11	
12	Build SFCC-91 to the five Jira ACs and the Figma `pdp/product-colour-picker` design, using a new
13	namespaced theme recipe plus a new atom and molecule under `ui-kits/`, consumed through a new
14	per-attribute render slot on the already-overridden `product-view` — with zero change to
15	`swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `translations/`, `theme/foundation/`, or any hook.
16	
17	## 1b. Decisions on record
18	
19	| # | Decision | Made by | When |
20	|---|---|---|---|
21	| 1 | Ignore the other developer's branch and PR #70; treat SFCC-91 as a fresh build | Marcel | 2026-08-31 |
22	| 2 | The PRDs' "Do not implement until confirmed" (SPR-26) is **stale** — proceed. `.docs/prd/plp.md` §5.4 and `pdp.md:219` need correcting by a human as a separate follow-up (skills are barred from `.docs/prd/**`) | Marcel | 2026-08-31 |
23	| 3 | Per-attribute render slot on `product-view`, **not** a `swatch-group` override. Marcel sanctions the second slot on that file as FED Lead | Marcel | 2026-08-31 |
24	| 4 | `Small/Rounded` variant is **out of scope** — no border-radius token exists in Tier 1 `theme/foundation/`, and there is no PDP consumer | Marcel | 2026-08-31 |
25	| 5 | **Pagination ships in Step 3** as designed — fixed 4-swatch window, prev/next chevrons, disabled at the ends, selection surviving paging. Found while verifying `40000307:13867`; it grew the molecule beyond the originally-approved shape and was approved on that basis | Marcel | 2026-08-31 |
26	| 6 | **Drop base's `backgroundColor={name.toLowerCase()}`** in the new component, with a Vitest guard pinning its absence. It uses the display name as a raw CSS keyword (unauditable, against `css.md`), exists to tint behind a *missing* image, and AC 5 guarantees this component never renders without one. Base keeps it; size still routes through the untouched path | Marcel | 2026-08-31 |
27	| 7 | **Keep the value type minimal — no forward-looking `kind` discriminator.** Cross-SKU "also available in" colours are SFCC-708's, and `conventions.md` says resist speculative abstractions. The molecule already takes a normalised `values` array rather than SFCC's `attr`, so SFCC-708 appends at the page level; add the discriminator then, when the behaviour is known rather than guessed | Marcel | 2026-08-31 |
28	
29	**SFCC-708 extension path (recorded so it isn't rediscovered).** `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` takes
30	`values: readonly {value, name, href?, imageUrl?}[]`, mapped from SFCC at the page (Step 4). Related
31	products from the future BM attribute are appended to that same array — **no molecule change
32	expected**. Two things SFCC-708 will have to resolve that this story does not: a discriminator, if
33	same-master and cross-product swatches must behave or look differently; and the group label, since
34	PRD-004 implies "Also available in" / "Only available in" and neither exists in the design.
35	
36	## 2. Scale — one branch, four commits
37	
38	The three modified files cannot be usefully separated. The theme registration is 4 lines and would
39	otherwise register recipes that don't exist; the slot has no value without its consumer, and the
40	consumer has no mount point without the slot. Two code-owner teams on one PR is normal and is what
41	CODEOWNERS is for.
42	
43	Hard Rule 10 (more than one protection tier) is satisfied by the manifest being fixed and
44	enumerated up front. The Tier 2 file must still be named in the commit body and the PR body.
45	
46	| Step | Loop depth | Why |
47	|---|---|---|
